decision.explanation: The provided evidence (pmid-20147967:f01) investigates K-Ras mutations in colorectal tumours and NIH3T3 cells. The specific variant KRAS Q597T is not mentioned in the text, nor is breast cancer mentioned as a disease context. The study tests other mutations (G12V, G12D, G13D, Q61H, L19F, K117N, A146T, R164Q) but does not provide any data on the oncogenicity of KRAS Q597T in breast cancer or any other context. Therefore, the evidence does not support, refute, or revise the claim regarding the oncogenicity of KRAS Q597T in breast cancer; it is simply absent.

citations.quote: Colorectal tumours (n=106) were screened for additional K-Ras mutations, phenotypes compared in transformation and Ras GTPase activating assays . . . To compare the transformation potential of the K-Ras mutants, therefore, NIH3T3 cells were transiently transfected with plasmids expressing wt K-Ras and the K-Ras mutations G12V, G12D, G13D, Q61H, L19F, K117N, A146T and R164Q . . . No foci were observed in untransfected cells or in cells transfected with wt K-Ras, whereas abundant foci were seen with each hotspot K-Ras mutation (Figure 3A)
